task_title: After Landing, Parking, and Securing (ASEL, AMEL)
objective: By the end of this lesson you can clear the runway, park safely, shut down and secure the airplane with the checklist, inspect it after flight, and write up anything that is wrong.
why: A flight is not complete until the engine is shut down and the airplane is secured [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. The ramp is full of people, propellers and distractions, and the next pilot depends on your write-up.

prereading.what: After-landing, clear of runway, parking, engine shutdown, post-flight, securing and servicing.
prereading.label: AFH 2-22 to 2-24

prereading.what: Ramp hazards, passengers on the ramp, standard hand signals, propeller hazards.
prereading.label: AFH 2-14 to 2-16

prereading.what: After-landing roll and when to do the after-landing checklist.
prereading.label: AFH 9-9 to 9-10

prereading.what: Inoperative equipment, placards, and maintenance entries.
prereading.label: PHAK 9-9 to 9-10

warmup: You just landed and are tired and happy. Your passenger wants a photo with the airplane. What three things could go wrong in the next five minutes?

key_terms.def: Two solid and two dashed yellow lines across a taxiway. Leaving the runway, taxi until the whole airplane is past them, then hold unless ATC says otherwise.
POH items done once stopped clear of the runway: flaps up, trim, lights, transponder and so on.
POH steps to stop the engine safely and secure the airplane.
A walkaround after shutdown to find leaks, damage, and servicing needs.
Anything wrong with the airplane that you found in flight or on the ground. Write it up so it gets fixed.
A label put near the switch or gauge of broken equipment that has been deferred under 91.213(d).
A device that holds the controls still so wind can't slam them.
Security Identification Display Area: an airport area where you must show an approved ID badge.

body.p: The landing is not over until you slow to taxi speed or stop clear of the landing area. Accidents happen when pilots relax right after touchdown [[24:180|AFH 9-9]].

bullets: Keep tracking the centerline and slow to normal taxi speed before turning off. Fast turns can damage the gear, tires and brakes [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

Exit without delay at the first available taxiway or as ATC instructs. Never exit onto another runway without ATC approval. At a towered airport, don't stop or reverse course on the runway without ATC approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

Unless ATC says otherwise, taxi until all parts of the airplane are past the runway holding position markings, even if that means entering another taxiway or ramp. Then hold unless ATC gives more instructions [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].
No ATC clearance is needed to cross the holding position markings when leaving the runway [[1:344|PHAK 14-10]].
At a towered airport, switch to ground when the tower tells you, and get a taxi clearance [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

callout.text: Do the after-landing checklist only after a complete stop beyond the holding position markings, unless the POH calls for an item during rollout (for example, flaps up on a short-field landing; positively identify the flap handle first). Pilots have raised the landing gear instead of the flaps while still rolling [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

body.p: Don't change frequencies, flaps or trim until you are clear of all runways [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].

check.q: After landing with no other ATC instructions, how far do you taxi before stopping?
check.a: Until every part of the airplane, including the tail, has crossed the runway holding position markings; then hold [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]] [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].

chunks.title: After-landing checklist and taxi to parking

body.p: Once stopped clear of the runway, use the POH after-landing checklist. Common items [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]:

bullets: Power: set per POH (for example, throttle 1,000 rpm, mixture leaned).
Fuel: switch tanks or fuel pumps off if the POH says so.
Flaps: retracted.
Cowl flaps: open or closed as temperature requires.
Trim: neutral or takeoff.
Lights: strobes off if not needed.
Avionics: frequencies and transponder set for taxi.

body.p: Picking a parking spot [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]:

bullets: Unless the area is supervised, choose a spot and heading where other airplanes' prop or jet blast won't hit you.
When you can, park headed into the existing or forecast wind.
After stopping, roll straight ahead a little to straighten the nosewheel or tailwheel.

body.p: Big airplanes can make exhaust blast or rotor downwash strong enough to make a light airplane uncontrollable [[24:52|AFH 2-15]]. Keep clear.
If a lineman marshals you in, follow the standard hand signals. At night, the Emergency Stop signal is used for all stop signals [[24:52|AFH 2-15]].

check.q: Why roll forward a little after stopping in your parking spot?
check.a: To straighten the nosewheel or tailwheel [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

chunks.title: Fly it step by step: shutdown and securing

body.p: Always use your airplane's POH shutdown checklist. Typical items, in order [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]:

bullets: 1. Parking brake: ON.
2. Throttle: IDLE or 1,000 rpm.
3. Turbocharged engine: follow the maker's spool-down procedure.
4. Magneto check: briefly switch to OFF at idle to check grounding.
5. Propeller control: HIGH rpm, if equipped.
6. Avionics: OFF.
7. Alternator: OFF.
8. Mixture: IDLE CUTOFF.
9. Magneto (ignition) switch: OFF when the engine stops.
10. Chocks in (release the parking brake per the POH).
11. Master switch: OFF.
12. Secure: control locks and anti-theft locks.

callout.text: Brake, idle, mag check, avionics off, mixture cut, mags off, chocks, master off, locks.

body.p: Checklists are memory aids so you don't skip critical items. You can do the steps and then read the checklist to confirm them, but you must actually use it [[24:36|AFH 1-15]]. 'After landing' and 'engine shutdown and securing' are on the AFH's minimum list of phases that need a checklist [[24:36|AFH 1-15]].
What the examiner expects (no numeric tolerances in this Task):

head: ACS element
Standard
rows: ACS PA.XII.A.S2
Park in an appropriate area, considering the safety of nearby persons and property.
ACS PA.XII.A.S3
Complete the appropriate checklist(s).
ACS PA.XII.A.S4
Conduct a postflight inspection and document discrepancies and servicing requirements, if any.
ACS PA.XII.A.S5
Secure the airplane.

check.q: Why turn the magnetos briefly to OFF at idle before using the mixture to stop the engine?
check.a: To check that the magnetos ground properly in the OFF position [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. A mag that doesn't ground can let the engine fire when someone moves the propeller.

body.p: The ramp can be busy with workers, passengers, trucks, airplanes, and even stray people and animals. The pilot is responsible for operating safely there [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

bullets: Most passengers have little ramp experience. Tell them to move only as you direct [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].
If they are not under your direct supervision, they should have an escort, for safety and ramp security [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].
Have everyone get out before refueling, and watch the fueling yourself [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].
A spinning propeller can kill someone it strikes [[24:53|AFH 2-16]]. Shut down fully before anyone gets out, and keep people away from the prop arc.
Part of your preflight SAFETY briefing: exit doors, how to open them, and the evacuation plan [[1:64|PHAK 2-25]].

callout.text: Before shutdown, tell passengers: 'Stay seated until I say. Then walk toward the back of the wing, away from the propeller, and wait for me.'
Watch for other airplanes taxiing or starting nearby. Their prop blast can blow debris into people and property [[24:53|AFH 2-16]].

check.q: Your passengers want to walk to the FBO while you tie down. What should you do?
check.a: Keep them under your supervision or have them escorted, and tell them to move only as directed [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

body.p: After shutdown and deplaning passengers, walk around the airplane [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]:

bullets: Cowling: oil or fuel streaks; oil breather for too much oil.
Under the wings and other tank areas: fuel stains.
Landing gear and tires: damage. Brakes: leaking hydraulic fluid.
Cowling inlets: obstructions.

body.p: Servicing [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]:

bullets: Check oil and bring it to the POH level.
Fuel based on the next use. If the airplane will sit, filling the tanks helps prevent water condensation inside them.
If another flight is planned, fuel for that flight's needs.

body.p: The fuller the tanks, the less room for condensation. Full tanks also slow the aging of rubber tanks and sealant [[24:47|AFH 2-10]].

callout.text: Do the postflight like a preflight for the next pilot. Leaks and damage are easiest to spot right after a flight.

check.q: Name three things to look for on a postflight walkaround.
check.a: Any three of: oil or fuel streaks on the cowling, excess oil at the breather, fuel stains under the wings, damaged gear or tires, leaking brake fluid, blocked cowl inlets [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

body.p: The PIC decides whether the airplane is safe to fly and must stop the flight if unairworthy mechanical, electrical or structural problems occur [[60:436|14 CFR 91.7]]. The owner or operator must get discrepancies repaired [[60:520|14 CFR 91.405]]. They can't fix what they don't know about, so you must report it.
What to document after a flight:

bullets: Anything that failed or acted oddly in flight (a flickering gauge, rough engine, radio static).
Anything found on the postflight walkaround.
Servicing needed: oil added or low, fuel needed.

body.p: Where it goes: an entry in the maintenance record or the discrepancy record provided for that purpose [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]]. At a flight school this is usually the squawk sheet or system the school uses.
Inoperative equipment rules:

bullets: Maintenance deferrals are not used for inflight discrepancies. Use the POH procedures for those [[1:239|PHAK 9-9]].

Without an MEL, an item may be deferred only if it is not required, is deactivated or removed, is placarded INOPERATIVE, and a pilot or mechanic decides it is not a hazard [[60:493|14 CFR 91.213(d)]].
If the deactivation involves maintenance, a certificated mechanic must do it and record it [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].
Placarded inoperative items must be repaired, replaced, removed or inspected at the next required inspection [[60:521|14 CFR 91.405(c)]].

callout.text: Only a pilot with at least a private pilot certificate may approve an airplane for return to service after preventive maintenance [[60:132|14 CFR 43.7(f)]]. As a student, report the problem; don't fix it yourself.
Write squawks so the mechanic can find the problem: what, when, where, and conditions. Example: 'Left fuel gauge reads empty with tank full, steady in flight and on the ground.'

check.q: In cruise the oil pressure needle flickered twice, then was normal. Do you need to write it up?
check.a: Yes. Report anything that acted abnormally so the owner can have it repaired [[60:520|14 CFR 91.405]]; record it in the maintenance or discrepancy record [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].

chunks.title: Securing the airplane and airport security

body.p: Hangar it or tie it down, secure the flight controls, and put security locks in place [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

head: Tie-down type
How to secure
rows: Chains
Not flexible. Don't pull them tight; leave a little movement to avoid structural damage [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]
Ropes
Flexible. Can be cinched reasonably to the tie-down rings [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]

body.p: Also consider [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]: pitot tube cover, cowling inlet covers, rudder gust lock, window sunscreens, and a propeller security lock.
Hangars have hazards too. Leave enough room so the airplane can't hit the hangar, another airplane or a vehicle, and check it for damage after hangaring [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].
Airport security:

bullets: Some airports have a Security Identification Display Area (SIDA). You need an approved badge to be there [[33:173|AIM 2-3-15]].
Pilots or passengers without ID seen entering a SIDA may be reported to TSA and may face fines or prosecution. Brief your passengers [[33:174|AIM 2-3-15]].
Report suspicious activity through AOPA's Airport Watch Program, 866-427-3287 [[33:174|AIM 2-3-15]].
You must show your pilot and medical certificate to TSA if asked [[33:174|AIM 2-3-15]].
Lock the airplane and use anti-theft locks [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. Follow the gate codes and rules of the airport you are at.

check.q: Why shouldn't you pull tie-down chains tight?
check.a: Chains don't stretch. Leaving a little slack lets the airplane move a bit and prevents structural damage [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

body.p: After landing you are tired and relieved, passengers are talking, and the ramp is busy. This is when steps get skipped.

bullets: Distractions take your attention away from the job. A small problem can push out more important tasks [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].
Many cockpit distractions start as a minor problem, but cause accidents when the pilot stops controlling the airplane [[1:63|PHAK 2-24]].
No nonessential talk or actions until you are clear of all runways [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].
Pilots who don't take checklists seriously get complacent and rely on memory [[24:36|AFH 1-15]].

callout.text: If you are interrupted during the shutdown or securing checklist, start that section over. Finish securing before you chat, take photos, or check your phone.

check.q: Your friend starts asking questions as you roll out on the runway. What do you do?
check.a: Keep flying the airplane and taxi clear first. Nonessential talk and actions should wait until you are clear of all runways [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].

head: Error
Fix
rows: Turning off the runway too fast
Slow to normal taxi speed first [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Stopping before the whole airplane is past the hold lines
Taxi until the tail is past the markings [[7:7|AC 91-73B]]
Cleaning up flaps or trim while still rolling
Do the after-landing checklist only when stopped and clear [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Parking where prop or jet blast can hit you
Pick a spot and heading away from blast [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]
Shutting down from memory and missing the mag check or master switch
Read the POH shutdown checklist [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]
Letting passengers wander the ramp
Direct them, or have them escorted [[24:51|AFH 2-14]]
Chains pulled tight, or no control lock
Some slack in chains; install control and gust locks [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]
Leaving without writing up a problem
Record it in the maintenance or discrepancy record [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]]

check.q: You left the master switch on after a flight. What could happen?
check.a: The battery could drain overnight. The master switch is an item on the shutdown checklist [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]; reading the checklist catches it.

scenario.title: Sunset arrival with two friends
scenario.setup: You land at a busy towered airport at sunset with two friends. Ground clears you to the FBO ramp. A business jet is starting engines two rows over, a fuel truck is moving, and your friends are excited to take photos. The airport has a fenced SIDA area next to the airline ramp. During the flight, the left fuel gauge bounced between 1/4 and empty.

questions.q: Where and how do you park?
questions.a: Pick a spot and heading where the jet's blast won't hit you, into the wind if you can, and roll forward to straighten the nosewheel [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. Powerful aircraft blast can make a light airplane uncontrollable [[24:52|AFH 2-15]].

questions.q: Your friends reach for the door handles as you pull the mixture. What do you say and why?
questions.a: Stay seated until the propeller has stopped and you give the word. A spinning propeller can be lethal [[24:53|AFH 2-16]]. Then guide them away from the prop and other traffic, moving only as directed [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

questions.q: One friend wanders toward the airline ramp for a photo. What's the risk?
questions.a: Entering a SIDA without ID can mean a report to TSA and civil or criminal fines [[33:174|AIM 2-3-15]]. Brief passengers beforehand, and escort them [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

questions.q: You are rushing to get dinner. What do you still do before leaving?
questions.a: Complete the shutdown checklist, a postflight walkaround, tie-down with control locks, and lock the airplane [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

Write it up in the maintenance or discrepancy record so it gets repaired [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]] [[60:520|14 CFR 91.405]]. Fuel quantity indicators are required equipment for VFR flight [[60:486|14 CFR 91.205(b)]], so it can't simply be ignored.

skills.do: Taxi to and park in a suitable spot, clear of prop and jet blast and away from people and property, headed into the wind if possible.
skills.practice: On every flight, say out loud why you chose your parking spot and heading before shutting down.

skills.do: Use the POH after-landing checklist once stopped clear of the runway, and the shutdown/securing checklist at parking.
skills.practice: Chair-fly the after-landing and shutdown flows with the checklist until you can do them smoothly, then always read the checklist to confirm.

skills.do: Walk around after shutdown, look for leaks, damage and servicing needs, and write up any discrepancies.
skills.practice: Do a postflight walkaround after every lesson and fill out the school's squawk sheet, even if just 'no discrepancies, oil 6 qt'.

skills.do: Tie down or hangar the airplane, install control locks and covers, and lock it.
skills.practice: Practice tying down on chains and ropes. Show your CFI correct slack and knots, and explain each lock and cover.

quiz.q: When should you normally complete the after-landing checklist?
options: After a complete stop beyond the runway holding position markings
As soon as you turn off the runway and are rolling toward the taxiway
During the landing roll, once the nosewheel is down and the speed is slow
At the parking spot only, just before you shut down the engine
quiz.why: Do it only after a complete stop beyond the holding position markings, to avoid grabbing the wrong control [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

quiz.q: After landing, with no other ATC instructions, you should taxi until:
options: The main wheels are off the runway and onto the exit taxiway curve
The nose crosses the solid yellow lines of the holding position markings
You reach the parking ramp, unless ATC gives a different instruction on the way
All parts of the airplane are past the runway holding position markings
quiz.why: Taxi until all parts of the airplane are past the holding position markings, then hold unless ATC says otherwise [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

quiz.q: Do you need an ATC clearance to cross the holding position markings when exiting the runway?
options: Yes, always
Only at night
No
Only at non-towered airports
quiz.why: No clearance is needed to cross when exiting the runway [[1:344|PHAK 14-10]].

quiz.q: When possible, you should park the airplane:
options: Downwind, with the tail toward the wind direction
Headed into the existing or forecast wind
Tail into the wind, so the wind lifts the elevators
Crosswind, so the wind hits the side of the fuselage
quiz.why: Park headed into the existing or forecast wind when possible [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

quiz.q: Why is a quick mag switch check to OFF done at idle during shutdown?
options: To cool the engine
To clear the spark plugs
To check proper grounding in the OFF position
To test the alternator
quiz.why: It checks that the magnetos ground properly in OFF [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

quiz.q: How should tie-down chains be secured?
options: With some slack, not taut
Only on the tail
Chains should never be used
As tight as possible
quiz.why: Chains aren't flexible, so don't make them taut; allow some movement [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

quiz.q: Filling the fuel tanks when the airplane will sit unused mainly helps:
options: Keep the CG forward
Prevent water condensation in the tanks
Charge the battery
Lower insurance costs
quiz.why: Full tanks leave less room for condensation [[24:60|AFH 2-23]] [[24:47|AFH 2-10]].

quiz.q: As a student pilot, you find a broken cabin light on postflight. You should:
options: Fix it yourself as preventive maintenance and sign it off
Ignore it if it's daytime
Remove the bulb and fly
Write it up in the maintenance or discrepancy record
quiz.why: A student pilot can't approve the airplane for return to service after preventive maintenance; that takes at least a private pilot certificate [[60:132|14 CFR 43.7(f)]]. Record the discrepancy [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].

takeaways: Slow down, exit, and taxi until the whole airplane is past the hold lines. Then do the after-landing checklist.
Park clear of blast, into the wind if you can, and straighten the nosewheel.
Always read the POH shutdown checklist; finish with chocks, master off, and locks.
Keep passengers seated until the prop stops, then guide or escort them on the ramp.
Walk around after every flight and write up every discrepancy and servicing need.
Tie down (chains with slack), lock the controls and the airplane, and respect airport security areas.
cfi_notes: Students often start the after-landing flow on the runway. Insist on stopping past the hold lines first.
Have the student brief passengers on ramp behavior before engine start, not after landing.
Use the school's actual squawk sheet in class; practice writing clear, specific discrepancies.
Examiners often watch whether the applicant actually reads the shutdown checklist, checks mag grounding, installs control locks, and asks the passenger (examiner) to wait for the prop to stop.
Discuss what the school's policy is for grounding an airplane versus noting a squawk.
AMEL applicants: the AFH 2-23 shutdown list is generic; multiengine and turbocharged airplanes have added POH steps.

Sources differ: PHAK 9-12 says student pilots may not do preventive maintenance, but 14 CFR 43.3(g) only excludes sport pilots (outside light-sport aircraft). 43.7(f) requires at least a private pilot certificate to approve return to service after preventive maintenance. The lesson teaches the regulation.

AIM 4-3-21 defines 'clear of the runway' as all parts past the runway edge with nothing stopping continued movement past the holding position markings; absent ATC instructions, pilots are still expected to taxi past the markings and then hold.
gaps: Exact after-landing and shutdown items, rpm values, and spool-down times come from the airplane's POH/AFM.
Airport-specific security rules (gate codes, badge rules, escort policies) are set by each airport and are not in these sources beyond AIM 2-3-15.
The sources give no standard format for a squawk sheet or discrepancy record; the school's system should be taught.
Multiengine-specific securing items are not covered in the reviewed AFH chapter 2 text.

activities.title: True or false: getting off the runway

cards.s: Ground control's taxi clearance to parking also lets you cross any runway on the way.
cards.why: No. A taxi clearance to parking does not let you enter or cross any runway [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

cards.s: With no other ATC instructions, you taxi until the tail is past the hold lines, then stop.
cards.why: Yes. Once all parts of the airplane have crossed the markings, you hold unless ATC says otherwise [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]] [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].

cards.s: If the nearest exit is another runway, you may turn onto it without asking.
cards.why: No. You must not exit the landing runway onto another runway unless ATC authorizes it [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

cards.s: Turning off the runway at high speed can damage the gear, tires, or brakes.
cards.why: Yes. Slow to normal taxi speed before you turn off [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

cards.s: On a normal landing, raise the flaps during the landing roll to save time.
cards.why: No. Do the after-landing checklist after a complete stop beyond the hold lines. Do an item on rollout only if the maker recommends it, like flaps on a short-field landing [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

cards.s: At a towered airport, you switch to ground when the tower tells you, then get a taxi clearance.

activities.title: Shut it down in order
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the shutdown steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Magnetos: quick switch to OFF to check grounding
Magneto switch: OFF once the engine stops
Control locks and anti-theft locks: install

activities.title: Whose job is it?
activities.intro: Tap a job, then tap who does it.

items.t: Decide if the airplane is in condition for safe flight
End the flight if an unairworthy mechanical problem occurs
Write a problem found on your flight in the discrepancy record
Get placarded inoperative items fixed or checked at the next required inspection
Remove a broken item from the airplane
Do a deactivation that involves maintenance

activities.title: Ramp and tie-down: the safe move
activities.intro: Tap a situation, then the safe move.

pairs.r: Tell them to move only as you direct
Get everyone out and watch the fueling
Fill the tanks to limit water condensation
Leave a little slack so the airframe isn't damaged
Leave room around it, then check for damage

pairs.l: Fenced SIDA by the airline ramp
pairs.r: Stay out unless you have an approved badge

final_quiz.q: Look at the picture. You are leaving the runway in the direction of the arrow. Which lines are on the side where you will hold once you are fully across?
options: The two dashed lines
The two solid lines
The single yellow centerline
The taxiway edge lines
final_quiz.why: The solid lines are always on the side where the airplane must hold [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5]]. Leaving the runway, you cross the dashed lines first, keep going until every part of the airplane is past the solid lines, then hold [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]]. The picture shows this [[1:344|PHAK 14-10]].

final_quiz.q: You land at a towered airport. The first turnoff you reach leads onto another runway. The tower has said nothing about it. What should you do?
options: Turn onto the other runway, since it is the first turnoff and the tower said nothing
Stop on the runway and wait for instructions from the tower before moving again
Turn around on the runway and go back to a taxiway you passed, if no one is landing
Pass it and exit at the next taxiway, unless the tower clears you onto that runway
final_quiz.why: Exit at the first available taxiway or as ATC instructs. Don't exit onto another runway unless ATC authorizes it, and at a towered airport don't stop or reverse course on the runway without ATC approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

final_quiz.q: On a normal landing (the POH lists nothing to do during rollout), when should you start changing radio frequencies, flaps, and trim?
options: As soon as the nosewheel is down
Once you are clear of all runways
While turning onto the taxiway
Only after you shut down at parking
final_quiz.why: Nonessential radio calls and actions, such as changing frequencies, flaps, and trim, should wait until you are clear of all runways [[7:7|AC 91-73B]]. Do the after-landing checklist once stopped beyond the hold lines [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

final_quiz.q: You taxi onto a ramp with several open tie-down spots. A turboprop is running two rows over, and the wind is from the west. Which spot is best?
options: Clear of the turboprop's blast, nose pointed east
Right behind the turboprop, nose pointed west
Clear of the turboprop's blast, nose pointed west
Right behind the turboprop, nose pointed east
final_quiz.why: Pick a spot and heading where other airplanes' prop blast won't hit you, and park headed into the wind when you can [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. A west wind blows from the west, so point the nose west. Strong blast can make a light airplane uncontrollable [[24:52|AFH 2-15]].

final_quiz.q: You are stopped on the taxiway, clear of the runway. Which item belongs on a typical after-landing checklist?
options: Flaps up and trim reset to neutral or takeoff
Mixture to idle cutoff, while still on the taxiway
Master switch off while you are still taxiing clear of the runway
Control locks installed once the airplane has stopped on the taxiway
final_quiz.why: Typical after-landing items include flaps retracted and trim reset to neutral or takeoff [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. Mixture cutoff, master off, and control locks are shutdown and securing items done at parking.

final_quiz.q: It is night. A lineman with lighted wands is guiding you to parking. Which signal will he use when he wants you to stop?
options: The normal Stop signal
The Slow Down signal
The Cut Engines signal
The Emergency Stop signal
final_quiz.why: At night, the Emergency Stop signal is used for all stop signals [[24:52|AFH 2-15]].

final_quiz.q: During shutdown at idle, you turn the ignition switch briefly to OFF. The engine keeps running with no change at all. What does this suggest?
options: The magnetos are working normally, since the engine should keep running after the switch moves
The mixture is set too rich, so the engine keeps running on fuel left in the cylinders
The magnetos are not grounding in OFF, so the engine could start if someone moves the propeller
The alternator has failed, so the engine is running on battery power alone
final_quiz.why: This step checks that the magnetos ground properly in OFF [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. If the ground wire between a magneto and the switch is broken, the engine can start when the propeller is moved, even with the switch OFF. Stop it with the mixture at idle cutoff and have a mechanic check it [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]].

final_quiz.q: A friend with 800 hours shuts down from memory and says checklists are for students. What does the AFH say?
options: Checklists are optional once you have 100 hours, so experienced pilots can shut down from memory
Checklists are only needed in multiengine airplanes, because singles are too simple
Pilots who skip checklists get complacent, and shutdown and securing should use a checklist
You must read each item before doing it, never after, and never from memory at all
final_quiz.why: Pilots who don't take checklists seriously become complacent and rely on memory. Engine shutdown and securing is on the AFH's minimum list of phases that need a checklist [[24:36|AFH 1-15]]. Doing the steps first and then checking them with the list is fine.

final_quiz.q: You pull the mixture to idle cutoff. Your passenger opens her door to hop out for a photo while the propeller is still turning. What do you do?
options: Tell her to stay seated until the propeller stops, then lead her away from it
Let her go if she walks toward the front of the airplane, away from the cockpit
Let her go, since the engine is already shutting down and the propeller is slowing
Taxi forward a little so she can step out onto the ramp where the ground is clear
final_quiz.why: A spinning propeller can kill someone it strikes [[24:53|AFH 2-16]]. Passengers new to the ramp should move only as you direct [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

final_quiz.q: Which set of checks matches the AFH postflight walkaround?
options: Propeller balance, battery voltage, and tire pressure readings taken with a gauge
Oil or fuel streaks at the cowling, fuel stains under the wings, and leaking brake fluid
Compass card, ELT battery date, and registration checked against the logbooks
Seat belts, seat rails, and door seals only, since the outside is checked before flight
final_quiz.why: The AFH postflight walkaround looks for oil or fuel streaks around the cowling, excess oil at the breather, fuel stains under the wings, gear and tire damage, leaking brake fluid, and blocked cowling inlets [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

final_quiz.q: On postflight you find the landing light is broken. The airplane has no MEL, and the light is not required for tomorrow's day VFR flight. What must happen to defer it?
options: Just note it on the squawk sheet and have the next pilot read it; nothing else is needed
Put an INOPERATIVE placard on it and leave it connected; nothing else is needed
It can't be deferred without an MEL, so the airplane must stay grounded until it is fixed
Deactivate or remove it, placard it INOPERATIVE, and have a pilot or mechanic decide it is not a hazard
final_quiz.why: Without an MEL, a non-required item may be deferred if it is removed or deactivated, placarded INOPERATIVE, and a pilot or mechanic decides it is not a hazard [[60:493|14 CFR 91.213(d)]]. Removal, or deactivation that involves maintenance, must be done by certificated maintenance personnel [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].

final_quiz.q: In cruise, the alternator warning light comes on. What guides what you do while still in the air?
options: The POH/AFM procedures, then a write-up after landing
The airplane's MEL deferral list
The 91.213(d) deferral steps
Nothing until the postflight walkaround
final_quiz.why: Maintenance deferrals are not used for inflight problems; use the AFM/POH procedures [[1:239|PHAK 9-9]]. After landing, record it in the maintenance or discrepancy record [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].

final_quiz.q: At a big airline airport, your passenger has no airport badge. She walks through an open gate into a SIDA to photograph an airliner. What could happen?
options: Nothing, as long as she stays off the runway and away from the airliner's engines
Nothing, since she is with a certificated pilot who has briefed her on the rules
She may be reported to TSA or airport security and face civil and criminal fines
Only you get a warning letter from the FAA, and she faces no penalty of her own
final_quiz.why: Moving into a SIDA without authorization and displayed ID is prohibited [[33:173|AIM 2-3-15]]. People seen entering one without proper ID may be reported to TSA and face civil and criminal fines and prosecution, so brief your passengers [[33:174|AIM 2-3-15]].
